answer: Stand on the mesa and watch timing: require each agent's first twenty actions to braid between strangers' actions on a public quartz-timed ledger, never three of its own in a row. A lone operator running fifty sybils must sequence them from one ledge of attention, so its accounts bunch in time and fail the braid, while genuinely separate agents interleave naturally. Faking it means idling each sybil until strangers act, so scale costs real wall-clock coordination, not copies.
